meta.title: Directive (EU) 2016/343 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 9 March 2016 on the strengthening of certain aspects of the presumption of innocence and of the right to be present at the trial in criminal proceedings

items.heading: CHAPTER 1

items.text: This Directive lays down common minimum rules concerning:
items.heading: Article 1

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment:
There were several project of law amending the CCP in order to transpose, among others, the Directive.

Two of these projects were adopted by the Parliament, but were subsequently quashed by the Constitutional Court which decided that both laws were unconstitutional.

 

See the “history” of PL-x no. 373/2018 Draft Law for amending and supplementing Law no.135/2010 on the Code of Criminal Procedure, as well as for amending and completing Law no. 304/2004 on judicial organization.

The first attempt was the draft law adopted by the Parliament in 18 June 2018. The Constitutional Court in October quashed the entire project in October 2018 – see Decision no. 633/2018.

Afterwards, the Parliament worked again on the draft law and adopted once again in April 2019. Again, the Constitutional Court quashed in July 2019 – see Decision no. 467/2019.

 

Trying to avoid entering the politics, the reason for the interventions of the Constitutional Court (itself accused of bias and party pries with the political party which governed in 2018-2019) was that both draft laws were seriously amending the CCP in an obscure and non-juridical manner, under the false motive of transposing, inter alia, the Directive.

 

In the follow up, as the Directive is still not transposed (last update is on 19 September 2019 when the Parliament started third time the reexamination of the project) we will make reference to the last version of the draft project, although the entire law was considered unconstitutional.

items.text:
(a)

certain aspects of the presumption of innocence in criminal proceedings;

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: Some part of the provisions can be considered implicit and partially transposed, as correspondent national legislation pre-existed the Directive.

items.text:
(b)

the right to be present at the trial in criminal proceedings.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: Some part of the provisions can be considered implicit and partially transposed, as correspondent national legislation pre-existed the Directive.

items.text: This Directive applies to natural persons who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings. It applies at all stages of the criminal proceedings, from the moment when a person is suspected or accused of having committed a criminal offence, or an alleged criminal offence, until the decision on the final determination of whether that person has committed the criminal offence concerned has become definitive.
items.heading: Article 2

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment:
Since the Directive itself is not transposed, there is no delineation about the exact moment of application. We must mention that some provisions of Directive are to be found in national legislation, as we well see below.


See Article 4 from the CCP on the presumtion of innocence


Presumtion of innocence (benefit of the doubt)


(1) Any person shall be considered innocent until the establishment of his guilt by a definitive criminal decision.

(2) After the administration of the entire probation, any doubt in forming the conviction of the judicial bodies shall be interpreted in favour of the suspect or the accused person.

items.heading: CHAPTER 2

items.text: Member States shall ensure that suspects and accused persons are presumed innocent until proved guilty according to law.
items.heading: Article 3

provisions.textEn:
Presumtion of innocence (benefit of the doubt)


(1) Any person shall be considered innocent until the establishment of his guilt by a definitive criminal decision.

(2) After the administration of the entire probation, any doubt in forming the conviction of the judicial bodies shall be interpreted in favour of the suspect or the accused person.

The burden of proof


(2) The suspect or the accused person benefits from the presumption of innocence, being not obliged to prove his innocence, and has the right not to contribute to his own accusation.

items.heading: Article 4

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: We will make reference to the last version of the draft project, although it was quashed by the Constitutional Court.

items.text: 1. Member States shall take the necessary measures to ensure that, for as long as a suspect or an accused person has not been proved guilty according to law, public statements made by public authorities, and judicial decisions, other than those on guilt, do not refer to that person as being guilty. This shall be without prejudice to acts of the prosecution which aim to prove the guilt of the suspect or accused person, and to preliminary decisions of a procedural nature, which are taken by judicial or other competent authorities and which are based on suspicion or incriminating evidence.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

4. In Article 4, after para. 2, six new paragraphs are inserted, par. (3) - (8) with the following content:


"(3) During the criminal prosecution and the trial of the case are prohibited public communications, public statements as well as the provision of other information, directly or indirectly, from public authorities regarding the facts and the persons who are the subject of these procedures. People within the public authorities cannot refer to the suspected or accused persons as if they were guilty unless there is a final judgment on conviction to those facts.

items.text: 2. Member States shall ensure that appropriate measures are available in the event of a breach of the obligation laid down in paragraph 1 of this Article not to refer to suspects or accused persons as being guilty, in accordance with this Directive and, in particular, with Article 10.

items.heading: Article 5
items.subHeading: Presentation of suspects and accused persons

items.comment:
Relevant provisions are in Law no. 254/2013 (the Regulation for its application merely add to these).

At least Article 16 para. 6 from the Law, which leaves at the discretion of the judicial organs the decision on maintaining handcuffs, contradicts the requirements of the Directive.

items.text: 1. Member States shall take appropriate measures to ensure that suspects and accused persons are not presented as being guilty, in court or in public, through the use of measures of physical restraint.

items.text: 2. Paragraph 1 shall not prevent Member States from applying measures of physical restraint that are required for case-specific reasons, relating to security or to the prevention of suspects or accused persons from absconding or from having contact with third persons.

nationalActs.titleEn: Law no. 254/2013 regarding the execution of the punishments and of the deprivation of liberty measures ordered by the judicial bodies during the criminal trial

provisions.textEn:
(1) The use of handcuffs or other means of restraint is permitted only in situations where other measures of maintaining order and discipline among the prisoners have not resulted in any of the following situations:

a) to prevent escape during detainees' movement;

b) to protect detainees from self-harm or to prevent injury to other persons or damage;

c) to restore order and discipline, as a result of the opposition or opposition of the detainees to a disposition of the judicial bodies or the personnel of the place of detention.

(2) The means of immobilization that can be used for the purpose provided in para. (1) are established by the regulation provided in Article 15 para. (3).

(3) The use of immobilization means is allowed only for the duration for which it is strictly necessary.

(4) The use of the means of immobilization shall be done gradually, without exceeding the real needs of the inmates' immobilization, and shall cease as soon as the purpose of the intervention has been achieved.

(5) The use of the means of immobilization must be authorized in advance by the director of the penitentiary, except in cases where the emergency does not allow this, a situation which is immediately brought to the attention of the director.

(6) The judicial bodies evaluate the application, maintenance or removal of the means of immobilization, during the presence of the detainees before them.

Application of provisions


(1) The provisions of Title I, Title II, as well as of the chapter. II, IV-VI and IX of Title III, insofar as they do not contravene the provisions of this Title, shall apply accordingly, with the exception of the following provisions regarding:

provisions.textEn:
Use of immobilization means


(1) The use of the means of immobilization shall be done gradually, without exceeding the real needs of the inmates' immobilization, and shall cease as soon as the purpose of the intervention has been achieved, in compliance with the provisions of Article 16 of the Law.

(2) The standard procedures for intervention and immobilization are established by the regulation provided in Article 15 para. (3) of the Law.

(3) In the case of inmates immobilized on the bed, hospitalized in a sanitary unit, no metal handles may be used. The model of the means of immobilization on the bed used in sanitary units and the way of their use are established by the regulation provided in Article 15 para. (3) of the Law.

(4) The physical force may be used, according to the legal provisions, in the cases of self-defense, escape or active or passive physical resistance to a provision provided in the Law, this regulation and the subsequent normative acts.

(5) Any intervention shall be carried out in compliance with the principle of proportionality between the mode of intervention and the cause that generated it, without making unjustified use of violence.

(6) By decision of the general director of the National Prison Administration, the method of completing the register provided by art. 106 paragraph (1) lit. c) of the Law

items.comment:
Relevant provisions are to be found in the so-called body of law comprising the execution law (namely Law no. 254/2013 and the Regulation for its application). The provisions of physical restraint are incident even in the case of suspect or arrested person if taken into custody or pre-trial arrested (see Article 110 from the Law referring to the general provisions on convicts).


As a general rule, regarding especially handcufs, the judicial bodies evaluate the application, maintenance or removal of the means of immobilization, during the presence of the detainees before them (Article 16 para. 6 from the Law). See also ECHR, Popovici vs. Bulgaria, 2016 on this regard.

items.heading: Article 6
items.comment: Although the pre-existing legislation generally respected the requirements of the Directive, the Romanian legislator wanted to add several other provisions and mechanisms. See the provisions from the draft project, most of it redundant and useless and some literally affecting the conduct of the ongoing criminal trial.

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that the burden of proof for establishing the guilt of suspects and accused persons is on the prosecution. This shall be without prejudice to any obligation on the judge or the competent court to seek both inculpatory and exculpatory evidence, and to the right of the defence to submit evidence in accordance with the applicable national law.

provisions.textEn:
The burden of proof


(1) In the criminal action the burden of proof lies mainly with the prosecutor, and in the civil action, the civil party or, as the case may be, the prosecutor exercising the civil action if the injured person lacks the capacity to exercise or has limited exercise capacity.

(2) The suspect or the accused person benefits from the presumption of innocence, being not obliged to prove his innocence, and has the right not to contribute to his own accusation.

(3) In the criminal case, the injured person, the suspect and the parties have the right to propose to the judicial bodies the administration of evidence.

items.text: 2. Member States shall ensure that any doubt as to the question of guilt is to benefit the suspect or accused person, including where the court assesses whether the person concerned should be acquitted.

provisions.textEn:
Assessment of evidence

 

(1) Pieces of evidence do not have a value pre-established by law and are subject to the free discretion of the judicial bodies, based on the assessment of all pieces of evidence produced in a case.

(2) In making a decision the existence of an offence and on the accused person's guilt, the court decides, on a justified basis, on the basis of all the assessed pieces of evidence. Conviction is ordered only when the court is convinced that the charge was proven beyond any reasonable doubt.

 (3) A court sentence ordering a conviction, waiver of penalty, or delay of penalty may not be based decisively on statements of the investigator, of informants or of protected witnesses.

Presumtion of innocence (benefit of the doubt)


(2) After the administration of the entire probation, any doubt in forming the conviction of the judicial bodies shall be interpreted in favour of the suspect or the accused person.

provisions.textEn:
The rights of the accused person


During the criminal trial, the accused person has the following rights:

a) the right not to give any statement during the criminal trial, drawing attention to the fact that if he refuses to give statements he will not suffer any adverse consequences, and if he gives statements they can be used as evidence against him;

The rights of the suspect


The suspect has the rights provided by law for the accused person, unless the law provides otherwise.

Manner of hearing


(3) During the hearing, a suspect or accused person may use their right to remain silent in respect of any of the facts or circumstances about which they are asked.

items.text: 2. Member States shall ensure that suspects and accused persons have the right not to incriminate themselves.

provisions.textEn:
The rights of the accused person


During the criminal trial, the accused person has the following rights:

a) the right not to give any statement during the criminal trial, drawing attention to the fact that if he refuses to give statements he will not suffer any adverse consequences, and if he gives statements they can be used as evidence against him;

The rights of the suspect


The suspect has the rights provided by law for the accused person, unless the law provides otherwise.

Manner of hearing


(3) During the hearing, a suspect or accused person may use their right to remain silent in respect of any of the facts or circumstances about which they are asked.

Informing on the charges, explanations and requests


(2) The President of the panel explains to the accused person what the charge is about, notifies the accused person about the right not to make any statement, noting that what he declares can be used against him, as well as regarding the right to ask questions of the accused, the injured person, the other parties, the witnesses, the experts and to give explanations throughout the course of the judicial inquiry, when it considers that it is necessary

Right of witnesses to avoid self-incrimination


A witness statement given by a person who had the capacity as suspect or accused person before such testimony or subsequently acquired the capacity of suspect or accused person in the same case, may not be used against them. At the moment when they record the statement, judicial bodies are under an obligation to mention their previous capacity.

items.text: 3. The exercise of the right not to incriminate oneself shall not prevent the competent authorities from gathering evidence which may be lawfully obtained through the use of legal powers of compulsion and which has an existence independent of the will of the suspects or accused persons.
items.comment: According to the evidence system regulated by the CCP (See General Part, Title IV, Evidence, methods of proof and evidentiary processes) in case the suspect or the accused person decides to remain silent in relation to the criminal offence that he / she is suspected or accused of having committed, all the rest of the methods of proof and evidentiary processes remain unaffected. So, nothing is there to prevent the competent authorities from gathering evidence.

items.text: 4. Member States may allow their judicial authorities to take into account, when sentencing, cooperative behaviour of suspects and accused persons.

provisions.textEn:
Plea bargaining procedure

 

(1) When the accused person applies for the trial to take place in the conditions provided under Article 374 para. (4), the court shall hear him following which, after the arguments by the prosecutor and the other parties, shall take a decision this application.

(1-1) The accused person may recognise the facts and request the trial of the case under the conditions provided in Article 374 para. (4) and by authentic document.

(1-2) In the cases provided in para. (1) and (1-1), if the accused person is a minor, approval of his legal representative is also required.

(2) If it admits the application, the court shall ask the parties and the victim if they propose the submission of documentary evidence.

(3) If it dismisses the application, the court shall act according to Article 374 para. (5) - (10).

Settling the criminal proceedings


(10) When the court proceedings were implemented according to the requirements under Article para. (1) and (2), when the defendant’s motion that the trial take place in these conditions was dismissed or when the court investigation took place according to the requirements under Article para. (5) or Article para. (2), whereas the court retains the same situation of fact as the one described in the bill of indictment and admitted by the defendant, in case of conviction or postponing the service of the penalty, the limits for the penalty provided by law in the case of a penalty by imprisonment shall be reduced by one-third, whereas in the case of a fine, by one-fourth. In case of minor accused persons, the court will consider these aspects when choosing the educational measure; in the case of educational measures deprived of liberty, the limits of the periods for which these measures are provided, provided by law, are reduced by one third.

Parties to the guilty plea and its limits


(1) During the criminal investigation, after the formal filing of charges, the defendant and prosecutor can conclude an agreement as a result of the defendant pleading guilty.

(2) The effects of the guilty plea shall be subject to approval by the hierarchically superior prosecutor.

(3) The guilty plea can be initiated by both the prosecutor and the defendant.

(4) The limits of the guilty plea shall be set by prior written agreement from the hierarchically superior prosecutor.

(5) If formal charges have been filed against several defendants, a distinct guilty plea can be concluded with each one of them, without impact on the benefit of the doubt extended to defendants who have not concluded such an agreement.

(6) Underage accused persons may enter into guilt recognition agreements, with the consent of their legal representative, under the terms of this chapter.

Conditions for concluding a guilty plea


(1) The agreement for the recognition of the guilt can be concluded only in respect of the offences for which the law provides for the punishment of the fine or imprisonment for a maximum of 15 years.

(2) The agreement for the recognition of the guilt is concluded when, from the administered evidence, sufficient data are obtained regarding the existence of the crime for which the criminal action was initiated and regarding the guilt of the defendant. When concluding the agreement for the recognition of guilt, legal assistance is mandatory.

(4) The accused person benefits from a one-third reduction of the penalty limits provided by law in the case of imprisonment and a one-fourth reduction of the penalty limits provided by law in the case of a fine. For accused persons who are minors, these aspects will be taken into account when choosing the educational measure; in the case of educational measures deprived of liberty, the limits of the periods for which these measures are provided, provided by law, are reduced by one third.

items.text: 5. The exercise by suspects and accused persons of the right to remain silent or of the right not to incriminate oneself shall not be used against them and shall not be considered to be evidence that they have committed the criminal offence concerned.

items.text: 6. This Article shall not preclude Member States from deciding that, with regard to minor offences, the conduct of the proceedings, or certain stages thereof, may take place in writing or without questioning of the suspect or accused person by the competent authorities in relation to the offence concerned, provided that this complies with the right to a fair trial.
items.comment: According to the CCP, the only situations which can correspond to this provision would be the plea bargaining procedure or the guilty plea one (see below). But, even in these cases, the accused person is heard in front of the court (even if at this stage emphasis is made especially on the legality of these procedures and the valid consent of the accused person).

items.heading: CHAPTER 3
items.subHeading: RIGHT TO BE PRESENT AT THE TRIAL

items.heading: Article 8
items.subHeading: Right to be present at the trial
items.comment: We considered the provisions of Article 8 to be de facto transposed. It seems the Romanian legislator had another opinion and very recently, Law no. 228/2020 was adopted. According to the final memorandum of the law, it transpoed, inter alia, the provisions of Article 8 para 4 from the Directive (see in detail the comment on para 4).

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspects and accused persons have the right to be present at their trial.

provisions.comment:
According to the draft law project:


187. In Article 364, after para. 6 a new paragraph is inserted, para. (6-1) with the following content:

"(6-1) A person may be convicted of the offense only if he has been legally summoned for each phase of the trial or has entered by other official means in possession of information regarding the place and date of the trial was informed about the possibility of making a judgment in default or if it was represented by a lawyer elected or appointed ex officio and benefited from appropriate defense during the trial. "
provisions.textEn:
The accused person's participation in the trial and his rights


(1) The trial of the case takes place in the presence of the accused person. Bringing the accused person into custody is mandatory. The accused person who is deprived of liberty is also considered present when, with his consent and in the presence of the chosen or ex officio defender and, as the case may be, and the interpreter, participates in the trial by videoconference, at the place of detention.

(2) The trial may take place in the absence of the accused person if he or she is missing, is evicted from the trial or has changed his address without informing the judicial bodies and, following the checks, the new address is not known.

(3) The trial may also take place in the absence of the accused person if, although legally cited, he is unjustifiably missing from the trial of the case.

(4) Throughout the trial, the accused person, including if deprived of liberty, may request, in writing, to be tried in default, being represented by his chosen lawyer or ex officio. If the accused person in custody has asked to be tried for failure, the court may order, on request or ex officio, that he can make conclusions in the debates and be given the word through video conference, in the presence of the defender elected or ex officio.

(5) If the accused person considers it necessary, the court may order his bringing with him a warrant of appeal.

(6) The accused personmay make requests, raise exceptions and draw conclusions, including in the situation provided in para. (1) final thesis.

items.text: 2. Member States may provide that a trial which can result in a decision on the guilt or innocence of a suspect or accused person can be held in his or her absence, provided that:

(a)

the suspect or accused person has been informed, in due time, of the trial and of the consequences of non-appearance; or

Reopening criminal proceedings in case of an in absentia trial of the convicted person


(2) The following shall be deemed as tried in absentia: the convicted person who was not summoned to appear in court and had not been informed thereof in any other official manner, respectively, the person who even though aware of the criminal proceedings in court, was lawfully absent from the trial of the case and unable to inform the court thereupon. The convicted person who had appointed a retained counsel or a representative shall not be deemed tried in absentia if the latter appeared at any time during the criminal proceedings in court and neither shall the person who, following the notification of the conviction verdict, according to the law, did not file an appeal, waived filing an appeal or withdrew their appeal.

(2) The following shall be deemed as tried in absentia: the convicted person who was not summoned to appear in court and had not been informed thereof in any other official manner, respectively, the person who even though aware of the criminal proceedings in court, was lawfully absent from the trial of the case and unable to inform the court thereupon. items.text: 3. A decision which has been taken in accordance with paragraph 2 may be enforced against the person concerned.
items.comment: According to the general system regarding enforcement of judgments regulated by the CCP, once a judgment is final, it will automatically be enforced. This is valid even in cases where the trial took place in absentia. In cases where the legal requirements for such a trial were not actually present, the convicted person may request the reopening the criminal proceedings (see Article 466 et seq. CCP).

items.text: 4. Where Member States provide for the possibility of holding trials in the absence of suspects or accused persons but it is not possible to comply with the conditions laid down in paragraph 2 of this Article because a suspect or accused person cannot be located despite reasonable efforts having been made, Member States may provide that a decision can nevertheless be taken and enforced. In that case, Member States shall ensure that when suspects or accused persons are informed of the decision, in particular when they are apprehended, they are also informed of the possibility to challenge the decision and of the right to a new trial or to another legal remedy, in accordance with Article 9.

provisions.textEn:
Ensuring the order and solemnity of the court hearing


(4) When one party or any other person disturbs the court hearing or disobeys the measures taken, the president shall warn them to keep order in court, whereas if this is a repeated situation or the offenses are severe, the president shall order them to be removed from the court room.

(5) The party or the person who was removed from the court room shall be called in before the beginning of the debates. The president shall inform the former on the essential actions taken while they were absent and shall read to them the statements of persons heard in court. If the party or the person continues to disturb the court hearing, the president may order them again to be removed from the room, while the debates shall take place in their absence.

(6) If the party continues to disturb the court hearing also during the issuing of the court ruling, the judicial panel president may order for the former to be removed out of the room, in which case, the court ruling shall be notified to this party.

items.text: 6. This Article shall be without prejudice to national rules that provide for proceedings or certain stages thereof to be conducted in writing, provided that this complies with the right to a fair trial.
items.comment: The logic of the new CCP was to have several proceedings conducted in writing (e.g., the preliminary chamber, the plea bargaining procedure, the guilty plea etc.). After several intervention of the Constitutional Court, which considered that such proceedings hinder the right to a fair trial, the relevant provisions were amended and now the procedures are involve debates. In case of the plea bargaining procedure and the guilty plea one, there is no more court investigation on evidence, as one precondition is that regarding evidence, this will be restricted to documents.

items.text: Member States shall ensure that, where suspects or accused persons were not present at their trial and the conditions laid down in Article 8(2) were not met, they have the right to a new trial, or to another legal remedy, which allows a fresh determination of the merits of the case, including examination of new evidence, and which may lead to the original decision being reversed. In that regard, Member States shall ensure that those suspects and accused persons have the right to be present, to participate effectively, in accordance with procedures under national law, and to exercise the rights of the defence.
items.heading: Article 9

provisions.textEn:
Reopening criminal proceedings in case of an in absentia trial of the convicted person


(1) The person with a final conviction, who was tried in absentia, may apply for the criminal proceedings to be reopened no later than one month since the day when informed, through any official notification, that criminal proceedings took place in court against them.

(2) The following shall be deemed as tried in absentia: the convicted person who was not summoned to appear in court and had not been informed thereof in any other official manner, respectively, the person who even though aware of the criminal proceedings in court, was lawfully absent from the trial of the case and unable to inform the court thereupon. The convicted person who had appointed a retained counsel or a representative shall not be deemed tried in absentia if the latter appeared at any time during the criminal proceedings in court and neither shall the person who, following the notification of the conviction verdict, according to the law, did not file an appeal, waived filing an appeal or withdrew their appeal.

(3) In the case of the person with a final conviction, tried in absentia, related to whom a foreign state ordered extradition or surrender based on the European arrest warrant, the time frame provided under par. (1) shall begin from the date when, following their bringing into country, they receive the conviction verdict.

(4) The criminal proceedings in court may not be reopened when the convicted person had applied to be tried in absentia.

(5) The provisions of the previous paragraphs shall apply accordingly to the person against whom a court ruling was returned to waive the service of the penalty or to postpone the service of the penalty.

The motion to reopen the criminal proceedings in court


(1) The motion to reopen the criminal proceedings in court may be submitted by the person tried in absentia and shall be filed with the court that tried the case in absentia as a court of first instance.

(2) When the person trial is deprived of liberty, the motion may be submitted with the administration of the penitentiary, that shall refer it as soon as possible to the jurisdictional court.

(3) The motion shall be put in writing and must be reasoned as related to the fulfillment of the requirements provided under Article 466.

(4) The motion may be accompanied by copies of the documentary evidence which the person tried in absentia understands to use during the court proceedings, certified as copies of the original. When the documents are written in a foreign language, they shall be accompanied by their translation.

(5) When the motion fails to meet the requirements provided under par. (3) and (4), the court notifies the author of the motion that they should supplement it no later than the date of the first court hearing or, as the

Preliminary steps


(1) When the motion to reopen the criminal proceedings in court is received, a date is set for the hearing where the admissibility shall be examined in principle, whereas the president shall order that the case file be attached, as well as that the parties and main interested subjects of the proceedings be summoned to appear in court.

(2) When the person who submitted the motion to reopen the criminal proceedings in court is deprived of liberty, even in another case, the president shall order that the former be notified as related to the date of the court hearing and shall take action to publicly appoint a counsel.

(3) The person deprived of liberty shall be brought to court for the trial.

Court proceedings related to the motion to reopen the trial


(1) The court shall hear the arguments by the prosecutor, the parties and the main subjects of the proceedings, and examine whether:

a) the motion was submitted within the deadline and by one of persons provided under Article 466;

b) legal grounds were relied upon to reopen the criminal proceedings;

c) the reasons based on which the motion was submitted had not been shown in a prior motion to reopen criminal proceedings, that had been tried by the court of last resort.

(2) The motion shall be examined as a matter of emergency and when the convicted person is serving the prison sentence applied in the case whose reopening is applied for, the court may wholly or partially stay the enforcement of the court ruling and provide the reasons thereof and may order the convict to observe one of the obligations provided under Article 215 para. (1) and (2). When the service of the prison sentence has not begun, the court may order the convict to observe one of the obligations provided under Article 215 paar. (1) and (2).

(3) If the court finds that the requirements provided under par. (1) are fulfilled, it shall order in a court resolution that the motion to reopen criminal proceedings be admitted.

(4) If the court finds that the requirements provided under Article 466 are not fulfilled, it shall order in a sentence that the motion to reopen criminal proceedings be denied.

(5) The court report wherein the motion to reopen criminal proceedings is admitted may be challenged jointly with the merits.

(6) The court ruling that rejects the motion to reopen criminal proceedings shall be subject to the same legal remedies as the court ruling issued with the convict in absentia.

(7) Sustaining of the motion to reopen the criminal proceedings may result in the rightful reversal of the ruling issued in the absence of the convicted person.

(8) The court shall reopen the criminal proceedings by extending it also to the parties that had not submitted any application. The court may also issue a ruling in their respect, without creating for them a more difficult situation.

(9) Upon the sustaining the motion to reopen criminal proceedings, the court, ex officio or by request by the prosecutor, may order that one of the preventive measures provided under Article 202 para. (4), letters b) to e) be taken. The provisions of the Title V of the general parties shall apply accordingly.

items.heading: CHAPTER 4
Article 10
items.comment: No specific remedies for breach of the Directive are regulated. As we will show below, in cases where implicit and partial transposition is considered, general remedies apply.

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspects and accused persons have an effective remedy if their rights under this Directive are breached.
items.comment:
Regarding certain aspects of the presumption of innocence in criminal proceedings, as mentioned before, the Directive is not transposed in national law. Therefore, it would be logical that no effective remedy is provided.

Since some provisions (e.g., presumption of innocence, burden on proof) are implicitly and partially transposed by previous existing national legislation, remedies in this field can be subsumed to the general right to defence and the fair trial concept.

 

In the case of public references to guilt, as there are no provisions in national law, no current remedy is afforded, de lege lata.

items.text: 2. Without prejudice to national rules and systems on the admissibility of evidence, Member States shall ensure that, in the assessment of statements made by suspects or accused persons or of evidence obtained in breach of the right to remain silent or the right not to incriminate oneself, the rights of the defence and the fairness of the proceedings are respected.

provisions.textEn:
Exclusion of evidence obtained illegally


(1) Evidence obtained through torture, as well as evidence deriving from such may not be used in criminal proceedings.

(2) Evidence obtained unlawfully may not be used in criminal proceedings.

(3) The nullity of a document ordering or authorizing the production of evidence or based on which such evidence was produced triggers exclusion of that evidence.

(4) Derived pieces of evidence are excluded if these were obtained directly from evidence obtained unlawfully and could not be obtained in other way.

Assessment of evidence


(1) Pieces of evidence do not have a value pre-established by law and are subject to the free discretion of the judicial bodies, based on the assessment of all pieces of evidence produced in a case.

(2) In making a decision the existence of an offense and on a defendant’s guilt, the court decides, on a justified basis, on the basis of all the assessed pieces of evidence. Conviction is ordered only when the court is convinced that the charge was proven beyond any reasonable doubt.

(3) A court sentence ordering a conviction, waiver of penalty, or delay of penalty may not be based decisively on statements of the investigator, of informants or of protected witnesses.

provisions.comment: See also Constitutional Court decision no. 88/2019 on the unconstitutionality of letter a) from para. 4 as refferd to letter f) from para. 1.

Absolute nullity


(1) Always causing nullification is the violation of rules concerning:

f) legal assistance by a counsel for the suspect or defendant, as well as of the other parties, when assistance is mandatory.

(2) Absolute nullity shall be found to exist either ex officio or on request.

(3) Violation of legal rules stipulated in para. (1) letter a) - d) can be raised at any stage of the procedure.

(4) Violation of legal rules stipulated in para. (1) letter. e) and f) should be raised:

a) before completion of the preliminary chambers procedure, if the violation occurred during the criminal investigation or during the preliminary chamber procedure;

b) at any stage of the procedure, if the violation occurred during the trial;

c) at any stage of the procedure, irrespective of the moment when the violation occurred, when the Court needs to rule in a guilty plea agreement.

provisions.comment: See also Constitutional Court decision no. 554/2017 on the unconstitutionality of letter para. 2 regarding the ex officio possibility to raise the nulity.
provisions.textEn:
Relative nullity


(1) Violation of any legal rules except for those stipulated at Article. 281 shall cause nullification of an act when the failure to comply with the legal rule caused harm to the rights of the parties or the main procedural subjects, which can only be removed by nullifying the act.

(2) Relative nullity can be raised by the prosecutor, suspect, accused person, the other parties or the victim, when they have their own procedural interest in having compliance with the legal rule that was violated.

(3) Relative nullity shall be raised during or right after the act was completed or at the latest within the time frames stipulated at par. (4).

(4) The violation described at par. (1) can be raised:

a) before the end of the preliminary chamber procedure, if the violation occurred during the criminal investigation or the preliminary chamber procedure itself;

b) before the first hearing that has full procedure completed, if the violation occurred during the criminal investigation, when the court is to hear a guilty plea agreement;

c) before the next hearing that has full procedure completed, if the violation occurred during the criminal trial.

(5) Relative nullity shall be disregarded when:

a) the interested party has not raised it inside the time frame required by law;

b) the interested party has specifically waived raising that nullity.
